threats.description: User, retrieved, tool, remote, and model content attempts to elevate itself into a trusted instruction zone.
threats.mitigation: Canonical provenance derives trust from the runtime entry zone, preserves taint through derivation, and rejects elevation.

threats.description: Untrusted prompt content forges structural delimiters or sibling prompt segments.
threats.mitigation: Prompt manifest v2 emits one canonical JSON frame per segment and escapes content inside the frame.

threats.description: Context or derived data crosses tenant scope.
threats.mitigation: Manifest normalization and provenance derivation reject mixed tenant scopes.

threats.description: A compromised, retired, or revoked publisher key continues to authorize adapters.
threats.mitigation: Signed registry records support authenticated rotation, revocation, quarantine, and compatible rollback.

threats.description: A caller reuses a valid installation identity with forged capabilities or filesystem policy.
threats.mitigation: Execution authorization returns the registry's stored signed policy and ignores caller-supplied policy fields.

threats.description: An adapter with an incompatible protocol, schema, version, or permission set receives work.
threats.mitigation: The supervisor completes a bounded handshake and rejects mismatches or permission overclaims before dispatch.

threats.description: An unapproved extension enters the runtime process.
threats.mitigation: In-process execution requires a registry-issued active grant and an explicit trusted factory.

threats.description: An out-of-process extension gains broad access to runtime internals.
threats.mitigation: The runtime exposes only a bounded JSON-RPC stream over SandboxBroker.

threats.description: An extension or authorizer changes identity, capabilities, permissions, or response correlation.
threats.mitigation: Identity is immutable across authorization; handshake subsets and JSON-RPC IDs are checked fail closed.

threats.description: Crash or silent-exit storms create unbounded restart loops.
threats.mitigation: A global restart budget, exponential backoff, bounded handshake timeout, quarantine, and audit events cap recovery.

threats.description: An extension floods or corrupts the protocol stream.
threats.mitigation: Negotiated frame limits, bounded queues, strict JSON-RPC parsing, and timeout-triggered process closure fail closed.

threats.description: An extension inherits host environment state or requests undeclared secret access.
threats.mitigation: The environment is constructed from an allowlisted request and secret permissions require opaque scoped references.

threats.description: A caller invokes undeclared adapter methods or routes WASI work through an unrestricted process runner.
threats.mitigation: Dispatch checks signed capabilities and rejects WASI until a dedicated runtime exists.

threats.description: A trusted in-process adapter panics or returns oversized or invalid protocol data.
threats.mitigation: Panic containment, response validation, negotiated limits, and quarantine prevent a plugin failure from crashing the runtime.

threats.description: A caller sends data to an undeclared destination, purpose, tenant scope, or sensitivity level, or dispatches before decision evidence is durable.
threats.mitigation: Canonical capability and egress policy evaluates signed grants fail closed and the supervisor persists the decision before adapter dispatch.

threats.description: A sandbox request escapes the workspace through traversal or symlink aliases.
threats.mitigation: Canonical containment and component-by-component symlink checks reject unsafe paths.

threats.description: A sandboxed process opens undeclared outbound network connections.
threats.mitigation: The macOS reference backend uses a deny-default Seatbelt profile and rejects grants it cannot bind faithfully.

threats.description: A timed-out or cancelled process remains live.
threats.mitigation: Execution deadlines and cancellation terminate the process and publish a durable result category.

threats.description: A process exhausts runtime memory through unbounded output.
threats.mitigation: Output accounting terminates the process at a finite configured limit.

threats.description: A cancelled process leaves descendant processes behind.
threats.mitigation: Unix process-group cancellation terminates the complete descendant tree.

threats.description: A secret reference is resolved outside its tenant, destination, or purpose scope.
threats.mitigation: Secret leases bind the complete scope and material requests must reproduce it exactly.

threats.description: Secret plaintext leaks through serializable lease metadata.
threats.mitigation: Public leases contain only opaque references and scoped metadata.

threats.description: An extension declares secret access but starts without any broker-issued reference.
threats.mitigation: Extension startup rejects secret permissions when no opaque reference is supplied.

threats.description: A stale worker forges or commits an effect receipt after losing its lease.
threats.mitigation: Effect transitions require the current positive fencing token and matching tool/effect identity.

threats.description: A write effect with unknown external outcome is automatically redispatched.
threats.mitigation: Unknown write outcomes are terminal until explicit policy-driven reconciliation.

threats.description: Sensitive prompt or tool payload values cross an adapter boundary in plaintext.
threats.mitigation: Prompt and tool surfaces redact unclassified scalar values by default and honor explicit sensitivity.

threats.description: Credentials or secret-shaped values leak through trace attributes.
threats.mitigation: Trace attribute keys and values pass through deterministic redaction before export.

threats.description: A caller forges actor, tenant, or workspace headers to escape the scope bound to its authenticated credential.
threats.mitigation: Authentication binds a validated Actor to request context and handlers derive identity and scope only from that context in authenticated profiles.

threats.description: A static, expired, revoked, or otherwise invalid service credential continues to authorize API calls.
threats.mitigation: Short-lived Ed25519 credentials bind audience and scope; key and credential revocation fail closed and the legacy static token configuration prevents readiness.

threats.description: Delegation, impersonation, takeover, or break-glass hides the initiating principal from audit evidence.
threats.mitigation: Actor transitions retain the original principal and complete transition chain, and audit records store both effective and original identity with the credential ID.
